nodes.label: AddDbContextPool
nodes.rationale: Reuses context instances to cut construction overhead; requires contexts hold no per-request state.

nodes.label: Change Tracker (snapshot-based)
nodes.rationale: Snapshot comparison via DetectChanges has cost proportional to tracked entities; AsNoTracking avoids it for read-only queries.

nodes.label: DbContext
nodes.rationale: Acts as session, Unit of Work and Repository; not a long-lived singleton because it is not thread-safe and its change tracker accumulates state.

nodes.label: DbContext Scoped Lifetime
nodes.rationale: Scoped per HTTP request because DbContext is not thread-safe; singletons cause threading violations and stale tracked data.

nodes.label: Fluent API vs Data Annotations
nodes.rationale: Fluent API keeps entities EF-agnostic and exposes the full configuration surface; annotations reserved for simple cases.

nodes.label: SaveChanges() Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Wraps multiple statements in an implicit transaction so a single SaveChanges is atomic.

nodes.label: Clean-Architecture-flavored layering
nodes.rationale: Solution is shaped as Domain/Persistence/Application/Api, but CLAUDE.md states Application is an unused placeholder and controllers call AppDbContext directly (note: current EventsController uses Mediator commands/queries from EventsHub.Application, so this description appears stale).

nodes.label: EventsHubBaseController route pattern (api/v1/[controller])
nodes.rationale: All controllers derive from a shared base with [Route("api/v1/[controller]")] and [ApiController] so routing/versioning is uniform; new controllers should follow it.

nodes.label: Generated artifacts - never hand-edit rule
nodes.rationale: EventsHub.v1.json, EventsHubRpcClient.generated.cs and Persistence/Migrations are regenerated by tooling; hand edits would be overwritten.

nodes.label: Shared seeded SQLite test DB convention (GlobalTestSetup)
nodes.norm_label: shared seeded sqlite test db convention (globaltestsetup)
nodes.rationale: DB is seeded once per run and shared, so tests read existing rows (e.g. Events.FirstAsync()) instead of asserting hardcoded counts/IDs, avoiding ordering/seed-count coupling.

nodes.label: Startup MigrateAsync + SeedDataAsync (logged, never rethrown)
nodes.rationale: DB errors are logged but not fatal so the API still starts serving with whatever schema exists.

nodes.label: Api assembly loaded as MVC application part via typeof(WeatherForecastController)
nodes.norm_label: api assembly loaded as mvc application part via typeof(weatherforecastcontroller)
nodes.rationale: Program in EventsHub.Api is an internal top-level type, so a public controller type is used to get the assembly handle; separate port 5011 avoids colliding with the real API on 5001.

nodes.label: Hardcoded API URL in App.tsx (no env base URL)
nodes.norm_label: hardcoded api url in app.tsx (no env base url)
nodes.rationale: Known rough edge: first gap to close before adding more API calls or targeting a non-localhost backend.

nodes.label: AsSplitQuery / Cartesian Explosion
nodes.rationale: Avoids duplicated rows from multiple collection includes at the cost of multiple round trips and non-atomic consistency.

nodes.label: Domain Layer
nodes.rationale: Has no dependencies on other projects or infrastructure packages; compiles with only the base class library.

nodes.label: FluentValidation
nodes.rationale: Input validation at the boundary plus domain invariants in entities: intentional two layers of defense.

nodes.label: MediatR
nodes.rationale: Decouples API from handlers and centralizes cross-cutting behavior, at the cost of indirection and a commercial license in recent versions.

nodes.label: Infrastructure / Persistence Layer
nodes.rationale: Mapping lives in IEntityTypeConfiguration classes rather than data annotations to keep EF Core attributes out of the Domain.

nodes.label: Test Doubles and Mocking Boundaries (Moq, NSubstitute, Fakes)
nodes.norm_label: test doubles and mocking boundaries (moq, nsubstitute, fakes)

nodes.label: Bounded Context
nodes.rationale: Apply CQRS per bounded context only where benefits are visible; mixing with plain CRUD is healthy.

nodes.label: CQRS in Web APIs (HTTP verb mapping)
nodes.norm_label: cqrs in web apis (http verb mapping)

nodes.label: Dispatcher / Command & Query Bus
nodes.rationale: Optional convenience: decouples callers from handlers and hosts cross-cutting behaviors; direct handler calls are still CQRS.

nodes.label: Dependency Injection
nodes.rationale: Makes the Dependency Rule workable; avoid service locator anti-pattern and scoped-into-singleton captive dependencies.

nodes.label: Repository and Unit of Work patterns
nodes.norm_label: repository and unit of work patterns
nodes.rationale: Debate: DbContext already implements both; pragmatic middle path is repositories per aggregate on write side, direct DTO queries on read side.

nodes.label: Result Pattern vs Exceptions
nodes.rationale: Results for expected business failures, exceptions for truly unexpected ones; consistent convention lets the API map errors to ProblemDetails in one place.

nodes.label: Vertical Slice Architecture / Feature Folders
nodes.rationale: Hybrid recommended: Clean Architecture project boundaries with feature folders inside each project.

nodes.label: CQRS (Command Query Responsibility Segregation)
nodes.rationale: Writes need rich rule-enforcing models; reads need flat fast shapes. Separating them resolves model conflict, workload asymmetry and growing complexity, but moves complexity rather than removing it.

nodes.label: Code Coverage
nodes.rationale: Diagnostic signal, not a target; chasing percentages yields low-value tests.

nodes.label: Testing Pyramid (Mike Cohn)
nodes.rationale: Bulk of confidence from cheap fast unit tests; reserve slow E2E tests for critical paths.

nodes.label: Saga / Process Manager
nodes.rationale: No distributed rollback; compensating actions undo earlier steps. Choreography vs orchestration trade-off.

nodes.label: Clean Architecture
nodes.rationale: Business rules sit at the center; DB, web framework, UI are replaceable details. Targets coupling, poor testability, framework lock-in, unclear boundaries; costs more projects, interfaces and mapping code.

nodes.label: Dependency Inversion Principle
nodes.rationale: The load-bearing SOLID principle: without it Application would have to reference Persistence and arrows would point outward.

nodes.label: Dependency Rule
nodes.rationale: Source code dependencies point only inward; inner layers define interfaces, outer layers implement them, so compile-time arrows oppose runtime call flow.

nodes.label: DTO Boundaries and Mapping (Manual / Mapster / AutoMapper)
nodes.norm_label: dto boundaries and mapping (manual / mapster / automapper)
nodes.rationale: Entities should not cross the API boundary; manual mapping is the preferred boring default; AutoMapper risks runtime failures and has a commercial license.

nodes.label: When Not to Use Clean Architecture
nodes.norm_label: when not to use clean architecture
nodes.rationale: Too much for CRUD, prototypes, tiny teams, glue services; pays off for long-lived systems with real domain logic. Adopt valuable parts selectively.

nodes.label: Event Sourcing
nodes.rationale: Independent of CQRS; adopt only when auditability or temporal queries are genuinely required due to schema evolution, replay and privacy costs.

nodes.label: Evolving toward CQRS (staged approach)
nodes.rationale: Stages 0-6 from separating code paths to event sourcing; stopping at stage 2 or 3 is legitimate.

nodes.label: Outbox Pattern
nodes.rationale: Write event to outbox table in same transaction as state change; relay gives at-least-once delivery, so consumers must be idempotent.

nodes.label: Separate Read and Write Stores
nodes.rationale: Independent scaling and specialized storage at the cost of eventual consistency, projection code and rebuilds; synchronous dual write discouraged.

nodes.label: Single Database, Separated Models
nodes.rationale: Strongly consistent, low operational cost, most of the benefit; often the right final destination.

nodes.label: Git Squash (interactive rebase / squash merge)
nodes.rationale: Cleans history before merge; rewriting shared branches requires team agreement and force-with-lease.

nodes.label: Graphify git hooks (post-commit/post-checkout)
nodes.rationale: AST-only rebuild is free and never fails the commit; hooks are per-machine since .git/hooks is untracked.

nodes.label: .graphifyignore
nodes.rationale: Excludes build output, node_modules and NSwag-generated code so the graph reflects real code.

nodes.label: EventsHub.nswag Codegen Config
nodes.rationale: runtime must match SDK (Net100); generateExceptionClasses must be true or ApiException is missing once real operations exist.

nodes.label: NSwag CLI as dotnet local tool
nodes.norm_label: nswag cli as dotnet local tool
nodes.rationale: Local tool manifest keeps pipeline reproducible per machine/CI without mutating global state.

nodes.label: Global CLI install, repo-scoped init model
nodes.norm_label: global cli install, repo-scoped init model
nodes.rationale: Neither tool is a project dependency; nothing goes in csproj/package.json, only initialized output is committed.
